This misstates which legs will label: `codex` is an **agent-runner** provider, not chat-completions — `CodexProvider(AgentRunnerProvider)` at `scripts/reviewer.py:1548`, and `docs/PR_METADATA_CHECKS.md`'s matrix lists `codex` under agent-runner with complexity as "⚠️ no-op". Only the `anthropic` leg will call `set_pr_complexity` and apply `complexity:*`; the codex, claude-code, and cursor legs each log the no-op warning. Runtime behavior is the designed degradation, but this comment — repeated in the PR description — will make a maintainer read the missing label from the codex leg as a bug.

```suggestion
          # and applies `complexity:low|medium|high`. The chat-completions leg
          # (anthropic) performs the assessment; agent-runner legs
          # (claude-code, cursor, codex) log a no-op warning by design.
```

The `ready` → `AIReview` rename is complete inside this file — including the `empty_reason` sentinel, renamed in lockstep on the emit (`line 136`) and the gate `if:` (`line 382`) — but it orphans the docs that tell contributors how to trigger the dogfood: `AGENTS.md:315` still says the workflow is "label-gated on `ready`", and the citations at lines 56 and 363 now point at a `docs/TRIGGER_MODES.md` heading that still reads "…labelled `ready`…" (`docs/TRIGGER_MODES.md:64`). Anyone following AGENTS.md — or this PR's own test plan, which says to apply `ready` — gets a silent grey skip with no error. Update `AGENTS.md`, and either rename the TRIGGER_MODES heading or point the citations back at the real one.

## Verdict

The complexity-labeling wiring is correct and the rename was executed thoroughly — but two `warning`s should land before merge: the new comment misstates **which legs actually apply the label** (codex is agent-runner, not chat-completions), and the `ready` → `AIReview` rename orphans the docs that tell contributors how to trigger the dogfood.

## What I verified

- `complexity-labels-enabled` / `complexity-label-prefix` are real, pre-existing `action.yml` inputs (`action.yml:118-125`, env-wired at `action.yml:325-326`) — no silent no-op from undeclared inputs.
- The runtime's `label-gate` matching is case-insensitive (`scripts/reviewer.py:5158-5161`), so `label-gate: AIReview` agrees with the scope job's case-insensitive `"aireview"` grep — the defense-in-depth comment holds.
- The `no-ready-label` → `no-gate-label` sentinel was renamed on **both** sides (emit at line 136, gate `if:` at line 382) — no dangling consumer anywhere in the repo (`docs/TRIGGER_MODES.md:190` uses its own self-consistent example).
- The agent-runner no-op warning the new comment cites is real (`build_agent_runner_noop_warning`, `scripts/reviewer.py:6435-6442`) and documented.
